title: GitLab MCP Server -- T1190 no-host-bind unauthenticated PAT-backed mutation endpoint
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-44895 (GHSA-8jr5-6gvj-rfpf,
CVSS 9.2 CRITICAL), a self-reported advisory for `mcp-gitlab-server`,
which lets an AI agent talk directly to GitLab.

Prior to 0.6.0, `src/transport.ts`'s HTTP transport shipped with no
authentication layer and a wildcard `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on
every response. The `httpServer.listen(port)` call at line 97 passes no
host argument, so Node.js defaults the bind to `0.0.0.0` -- exposed on
every interface, not just loopback. Any unauthenticated caller reaching
`/sse` or `/messages?sessionId=<id>` could invoke mutation-capable
GitLab operations (the advisory's own PoC reaches `delete_repository`
and `push_files`) backed by the operator's own
`GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` -- with the wildcard CORS header,
even a malicious web page the operator merely visits in a browser could
reach it cross-origin.

Detection logic flags a request to either affected endpoint invoking one
of the destructive/mutating tool names, with no bearer credential
present -- the specific combination of endpoint + mutation-capable
operation + missing auth is what distinguishes this from routine,
authenticated agent traffic once the fix's auth requirement is active.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (yoda-digital,
via GHSA and NVD), fixed in 0.6.0 (requires `MCP_GITLAB_AUTH_TOKEN` when
`USE_SSE=true`, binds to `127.0.0.1` by default, restricts CORS to
localhost, and validates the Authorization header).
